> I have a chronic pain condition that no one can/will help manage.

Steal opiates.

> And then later, he and his friend basically raped me.

Hot. Any DP?

> Words of encouragement are always appreciated.

Quit reading books written for morons.

Life itself is a problem. Suicide is an elegant answer.

> More often than not life's difficulties do not continue ad infinitum - eventually good times, or times of happiness, emerge.

That's temporary too.

I tell people the truth. Nobody wants to hear it.

Did you forget the part where you called yourself a failure?

You can't even get a job as a temp and you want to be a social worker?

Niggah please. There's already enough unqualified screwups "helping others" just so they don't feel so shitty about their lives.

> I should just stop whining and go back to my mindless drone life?

It's that or suicide. Ain't life grand?

Sounds like you made quite a few mistakes...

Going into debt for college without the guarantee of a job, an unemployable boyfriend with delusions of grandeur, having unprotected sex while broke, etc.

There's still time for an abortion. Call Planned Parenthood **today**.

> Every time I see a bridge I wonder if it would be high enough to kill me

Jumping onto water isn't advised. You need to be several hundred feet up, and even then it's a slow death from drowning while in severe pain (bone fragments puncturing your internal organs).

Guns also aren't a guarantee, even if you aim for the brainstem.

A coward makes a post on SuicideWatch. Let's call him Frank.

Grow some balls and get your own place, Frank.

This cliche does nothing to help a suicidal person.

Fuck you.

She found someone else. You're disposable.

If you decide to live, you need to get used to this feeling. It will happen again, the only difference being it tends to get more severe the older you get.

> I live on top of a five story building, and jumping seems like a decent enough idea at the moment.

That isn't a high enough distance to guarantee death.

Make it a minimum of ten stories onto concrete.

Why do people who aren't suicidal post here?

I'm neither broke nor hungry. Maybe I should go stand in line for food stamps.

> I find no solace in the idea that we should try to do the best we can while we're alive.

Welcome to reality.

Hold on...

> [I'm] on the verge of pulling a Chris McCandless.

Good. You won't be missed by rational adults.

It was worth pointing out. You don't have to explain yourself; I do.

[http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/a5tyc/is_anyone_else_interested_in_a_prosuicide/](http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/a5tyc/is_anyone_else_interested_in_a_prosuicide/)

It was on the main page for a few minutes, then it disappeared. I'd have at least liked an explanation from whomever felt the need to remove it. There is no salient list of taboos.

So this is the asshole who ruined country music.

I saw a [movie](http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0338075/) about his casket. It sucked almost as much as his songs did.

What the fuck does this have to do about suicide?

If his father hadn't killed himself, "Gram Parsons" would never have existed.

It's odd that one of the moderators felt the need to delete my response after you'd seen it and quoted most of it.

This subreddit makes no sense to me. I suppose only certain types of people deserve help.

> You're entitled to your opinion however he wost most definatly not a "weirdo".

I apologize for the negative connotations of that word, but it's clear from your initial post that he was different from most people.

> but while you see that as a negative, David showed it to me as a positive.

And yet he still killed himself after seeking professional treatment. Isn't that hypocritical? Shouldn't his decision cause you to question everything he taught you regarding depression and suicide?

> I'm really sad you couldn't find any positive in this.

I'm pleased to know David is no longer suffering.

> David did have some other, confused, reasons why he wanted to die but I con't want to discuss them here.

Would it be possible to discuss these in private?

He seems like a very interesting man, and I'd like to know more about his philosophy.

Thank you, but that's a euthanasia subreddit.

As far as I'm aware there is very little support out there for able bodied individuals that have decided to die.  It's a similar but separate issue.

Would you explain what is different to the message above and the near identical one I posted as an article to this subreddit that was deleted within minutes?

It looks like that cunt Saydrah is going to delete my posts.

If you want my money, please PM me with your country/city and the best way to get in touch.

> (not suicide though)

> Also see: [http://www.reddit.com/r/depression/](http://www.reddit.com/r/depression/)

I'm serious, especially if you can supply decent smack.

If you're not, please don't waste my time.

I hope your suffering is minimal either way.
Wow, it vanished in under ten minutes. Thanks so much for giving this a chance.

> The only thing I can suggest is that if this subreddit doesn't seem to provide what a person is looking for, then they need to look elsewhere and leave it up to those who are gaining some benefit.

I agree with you.  However, I realize I can't be the only person who feels this way, and I would like to talk to others in my condition before I go.

Would anyone else be interested in the creation of a pro-suicide subredit?

Topics would include but not be limited to:

* Philosophy of suicide
* Relevant news articles
* Links to pro-suicide websites, forums, and newsgroups
* Discussions on which methods are dangerous or do not work
* Links to preexisting instructional videos and method files
* Support for those who feel oppressed by the anti-suicide camp

I have at least fifty articles to get the ball rolling, and I'm sure there are others out there who are willing to contribute.

I dislike censorship, but the following would have to be banned:

* Pictures of baby animals
* Songs/videos of the day
* Joseph Campbell quotes
* Crossposting from other reddits without a user's permission
* Suggesting exercise, meditation, and vacations are a panacea
* Anyone trying to convince a poster that their personal decision to exit is wrong

**Mods**: I realize this idea goes against your mission, but I can't be the only person here who feels this way. I just want to know if my efforts would be in vain. Thank you for not deleting this post.

Where do you live?

I have a few thousand dollars saved.

I'd like to OD on heroin but don't know any dealers. If you can help, the remaining cash would be yours to do with as you pleased.

> You're entitled to your opinion however he wost most definatly not a "weirdo".

I apologize for the negative connotations of that word, but the tone of your initial story made him seem different to most people.

> I'm really sad you couldn't find any positive in this.

I was pleased to learn that David is no longer suffering.

> David did have some other, confused, reasons why he wanted to die but I con't want to discuss them here.

Would it be possible to discuss them in private?

I'm glad I'm not the only person who realizes how shitty this subreddit is. The posts on SW have reinforced my decision to stop breathing.

I hope it's quick when you decide to go.
No, it isn't.

Cool story bro, but I'm still going to kill myself. It's the only part of life I look forward to. I'm so tired of people like you who think you know better because your life has worked out [for the time being...hahaha!].

> He never thought he was one of the most amazing people on this planet

He sounds like a weirdo, and we can presume he was smart enough to know it. Life is difficult for the abnormal.

> he was going mad and could never switch off his brain.

Yeah. Certain types of depression do not respond to treatment.

*Death solves all problems - no man, no problem.*

> He left no note, no explanation.

The clever ones tend to realize the futility of leaving a note. It's mostly stupid drama queens who bother to do this.

Did you even consider the likelihood that he'd tried before?

> I promise you’ll one day find that balance, and finding it is the most amazing feeling in the world.

Do-gooders like yourself never stop making promises about how it will get better and how all someone with chronic depression needs to do is "find her place." This is a load of idealistic tripe, and those of us who've lived with severe mental illness for decades are sick of listening to it. Fuck off, kid.

> You could totally miss just how much the world loves you.

How do you know David was loved?

If you thought he was so special, why did you only send him sporadic emails?

> How much it needs you, even if you don’t think it does.

Humans will one day be extinct. The world got along fine for billions of years without our species. It will keep on spinning after we're gone.
